newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen futures end flat after paring losses.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen futures end flat after paring losses.

text.p: Key December three-month euroyen deposit rate futures ended Thursday's TIFFE day session flat, after erasing losses on short-covering.
Day session turnover for the key contract was 69,169 lots.

Selling emerged in the afternoon following remarks by Jiro Ushio, chairman of the Japan Association of Corporate Executives, that a review of Japan's monetary policy may get under way from this summer, traders said.
"It is about time that discussions (over the review of monetary policy) started," Ushio was quoted as saying by Jiji news agency.

Before Ushio's remarks were reported, the December had recovered to 99.03 from an intraday low of 99.00 following the Nikkei 225 stock average's fall into negative territory, traders said. The Nikkei ended down 37.40 points, or 0.20 percent, at 18,698.07, after rising as high as 18,982.70.
"The December fell back to 99.00 on Ushio's remarks but recovered on short-covering by the close," said a trust bank trader.

Traders said the mood was bearish after Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Wednesday that a rise in confidence about Japan's economy could lead to concerns about price rises. "Yesterday's remarks by Matsushita had lingering impact. Ushio's remarks just aggravated the market's nervousness," said a city bank trader.

Shorter interest rate swap rates edged up as some banks paid two- to three-year fixed interest rates. Two-year IRS rates were quoted at 1.04/1.08 percent, up from 1.02/1.06 percent on Wednesday. Three-year IRS rates were quoted at 1.31/1.35 percent, up from 1.29/1.33 percent on Wednesday.
The BOJ drained a net 200 billion yen from the money market against a projected fund surplus of about 410 billion yen.
Call money remained well-bid despite the BOJ's accommodative stance due to strong fund demand ahead of the "Golden Week" holiday period which starts next week.
The start of "T-plus-three" (T+3) rolling settlement for JGBs was partly responsible for fund shortages, traders said.
Starting with JGB trades done on April 21, settlement is to take place three business days after a trade.
Under the old "T-plus-seven" (T+7) rolling settlement, JGB settlement took place seven business days after a trade.

Settlements of JGB trades done on April 15 under the old T+7 scheme and those done on April 21 under the new T+3 scheme took place simultaneously today, resulting in greater-than-usual fund demand linked to bond settlement.
This overlap of T+3 and T+7 settlements will last until next Wednesday.

About 150 billion yen worth of the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.57 percent. Another 20 billion yen worth were issued at 0.56 percent. Three-month CDs were issued at 0.57 percent on Wednesday.
